A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same propositional-probe and Hessian binding-subspace study. The text, equations, figures and appendices are readable and support matching retained, reorganized and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original probing, causal-intervention, generalization and adversarial-evaluation results, including Figures 4–7 and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds quantitative position/order analyses and detailed Llama results in Appendices I–J.

M1.justification: The domain probes, Hessian construction, binding metric and main lookup algorithm are retained. Appendix I adds an optional matched variant that constrains attributes to bind to unique entities, changing inference for that variant without replacing the main method.

E1.justification: Appendix I extends input coverage with controlled modifier-length variations, reverse and nested-clause constructions, and adversarial nested inputs. These are targeted extensions within the retained people-and-attributes task. Serial, parallel and coreference examples already existed in v1; English/Spanish and attribute-domain coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Prompting, DAS and random-subspace comparators are retained. Figure 13 adds the matched probe variant alongside original probes and prompting on the nested datasets, providing a limited new comparison. The detailed Llama results reuse existing comparator families.

E3.justification: The new position tests specify 512-context datasets generated using pools of 20 noun phrases and 20 verb phrases, and the gender analysis is additionally stratified by binding order. Existing main metrics, splits and model choices are retained; Llama was already identified as evaluated in v1.

E4.justification: Appendix I substantially expands validation beyond v1's selected similarity heatmaps and aggregate evaluations. Figures 11–15 systematically test spacing and ordering, analyze duplicate-entity errors, evaluate constrained matching, and examine nested-order adversarial and gender-bias performance. These directly investigate whether the probes capture semantic binding or positional shortcuts.

E5.justification: Standard-error reporting remains for the main results. However, v2 Figure 6 retains gender-bias error bars while dropping v1 Figure 7's explicit statement that they represent standard errors; the new appendix plots also leave their bars undefined. No new seed, repeated-run or significance-testing procedure is specified.

E6.justification: Appendix I adds substantial findings: 44% exact-match accuracy on nested inputs, duplicate-name assignments in 78% of failures, improvements from matching, and order-specific adversarial results. Appendix J supplies detailed Llama results previously only summarized as similar. Tables 1–2 largely redisplay v1 Figure 6 rather than establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 Section 5.1 explicitly posits orthogonality between the binding matrix and lexical-vector subspaces and states the resulting approximate binding-vector relation. Section 5.2 qualifies Hessian recovery as approximate and up to scaling, whereas v1 Section 4.1 described exact identification under bilinearity. No substantial new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain compositional propositional probes, Hessian-based identification of binding structure, generalization from templates to stories and Spanish, and greater faithfulness than prompting in the three studied adversarial settings. The rewritten introduction and conclusion preserve these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix I newly interprets binding as partly order-sensitive and suggests that this fragility may originate in the model's representations. Appendix C.1 adds a circuit-based explanation for shared perturbations and the layer-15 symmetric metric. Conversely, v2 removes v1's explicit warning that probes cannot certify faithfulness or guarantee reliability in other settings.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository address in Section 4 and explicitly identifies the probed activations as pre-layernorm activations. Appendix I documents templates and sampling details for its new tests. Existing hardware, runtime, domain inventories and DAS hyperparameters remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the discussion and citations contrasting contextual faithfulness with factuality probing by Burns et al. and Marks and Tegmark. It more explicitly distinguishes its compositional approach from earlier proposition probes and motivates Hessian estimation against dataset-limited alternatives. Most cited research is retained.

P1.justification: The exposition changes substantially from Hessian-first to probe-first. v2 rewrites the introduction and preliminaries, introduces an explicit task-definition section, separates probe construction from evaluation, and consolidates standard and adversarial evaluations in Section 6. This is extensive narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 replaces v1 Figure 6's compact result plots with Tables 1–2, removes the original conceptual Figure 1, redraws introductory diagrams, and adds Hessian-step and circuit diagrams. Appendices I–J introduce numerous result displays, alongside substantial changes to figure placement and manuscript layout.

improvement.justification: The controlled position/order analyses improve the evidence about what the probes measure and expose failures that v1's qualitative examples did not quantify. Clearer result tables, detailed Llama results and the code address also improve inspectability. These benefits are tempered by removal of the no-certification warning and an unresolved matching-result discrepancy: Appendix I reports 76% accuracy, while Figure 13 shows about 88% for the matched nested condition. Overall, the revision provides a useful but qualified quality gain.
